title: Reply: the Spirit's unction is real but unequal; Philippians 3 bears with the imperfect
source_text: XII. Resp. Verum quidem est Deum fidelibus omnibus Spiritum suum indulgere qui eos in verbi sui cognitionem ducit: eosque, ut inquit Joannes, unctionem habere a Sancto quae eos docet de omnibus. Veruntamen non omnes spiritum illum fidei et sapientiae aequaliter participant: Nec Deus illum omnibus et singulis aequali mensura dispensat: sed aliis majorem, aliis vero minorem spiritus illius copiam impertit: Neque unctio illa fideles omnes docet de omnibus simpliciter, sed saltem de omnibus quae vocationi cujusque congruunt, et ad cujusque salutem et cognitionem necessaria sunt, secundum statum et conditionem suam, et locum quem tenet in Ecclesia Dei. Unde fit ut qui fide, et rerum divinarum cognitione donatus est, quantum ad salutem sufficit, possit tamen in aliquo fidei capite errare, et aliquam verbi Dei partem non agnoscere. Ideoque Paulus ad Philippenses capite tertio, vult ut qui perfecti sunt ferant aliter sentientes, et tanquam cum fratribus communionem colant, interim dum Deus ipsis revelet illud ad quod nondum pervenerunt. Quotquot, inquit, perfecti sumus hoc sentiamus: quod si quid aliter sentitis, hoc quoque vobis Deus revelabit. Attamen in eo ad quod pervenimus, eadem incidamus regula, et idem sentiamus.
pass_a_gloss: Reply. It is indeed true that God grants his Spirit to all the faithful, who leads them into the knowledge of his word: and that they, as John says, have an anointing from the Holy One which teaches them concerning all things. Nevertheless not all share that spirit of faith and wisdom equally: Nor does God dispense it to all and each by an equal measure: but he imparts a greater supply of that spirit to some, and a lesser to others: Nor does that anointing teach all the faithful concerning all things simply, but at least concerning all things that suit each one's calling, and that are necessary for each one's salvation and knowledge, according to his state and condition, and the place he holds in the Church of God. Whence it comes about that he who is gifted with faith and knowledge of divine things, as much as suffices for salvation, may yet err in some head of faith, and not recognize some part of God's word. And therefore Paul to the Philippians in the third chapter wills that those who are perfect bear with those who think otherwise, and cultivate communion with them as with brothers, meanwhile until God reveals to them that to which they have not yet come. As many as are perfect, he says, let us think this: and if you think anything otherwise, God will also reveal this to you. Yet in that to which we have come, let us walk by the same rule, and think the same.
pass_b_english: Reply. It is true that God grants his Spirit to all the faithful and leads them into knowledge of his word, and that — as John says — they have an anointing from the Holy One that teaches them concerning all things.

Yet not all share that spirit of faith and wisdom equally. God does not dispense it to each by the same measure; he gives a greater supply to some and a lesser to others. Nor does that anointing teach every believer simply everything, but at least whatever suits each calling and is needed for each one's salvation and knowledge, according to state, condition, and place in God's Church.
So someone gifted with faith and knowledge of divine things enough for salvation may still err on some point of faith and fail to recognize some part of God's word.

That is why Paul in Philippians 3 wants those who are perfect to bear with those who think otherwise and keep brotherly communion while God reveals what they have not yet reached: As many of us as are perfect, let us think this; and if you think anything otherwise, God will also reveal this to you. Yet in what we have already reached, let us walk by the same rule and think the same.
